...SECOND INNINGS...

South Africa Women looked tired as the game progressed. They were beaten by an experienced group of opposition. The bowlers seem to lack a clear plan as all of them bowled a lot of freebies. South Africa Women now have a massive task on their hand. They have to bat their hearts out. They'll bank on Laura Wolvaardt or Marizanne Kapp to play a formidable innings. How will South Africa Women reply? Let's find out.

India Women have declared on 603! They were hoping for Richa Ghosh to get the triple-digit score but her wicket means now South Africa Women have to bat a tricky first session period. What an innings! What a start to the match. India chose to bat first and the foundation was laid by the openers, Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma who added 292 runs for the first wicket. The former fell on 149 but Verma went onto score a double century. Apart from the two, there were handy contributions from Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur and Richa Ghosh who scored fifties and took India over 600.

Hello and welcome to the action of Day 2 between India and South Africa. We saw a historic start to the match as runs were scored for fun on Day 1. India scored a record 525 runs beating previous best of 431 in a day in women’s cricket. The Chepauk pitch consists of invariably turn on most occasions but we saw red soil flat track easy to bat on. So good to bat that Mandhana and Verma added 292 for the first wicket. The former fell on 149 but her hard hitting partner scored a double century. India have Ghosh and Kaur in their 40s but the overall score have gone past the Proteas' imagination who look confused while bowling. South Africa will hope they take a few wickets as we might certainly see India declare sooner or later on Day 2. Stay tuned.
... Day 2, Session 1...

Looking at this series, South Africa Women have not been at their best in the field and with the ball so far. Apart from the first 10 overs, it was all India throughout the day. They tried to build some momentum but once the ball got old, South Africa Women got hammering from India in all the sessions. They took two wickets each in the last two sessions but overall it was really an ordinary bowling performance from South Africa. Even a lot of misfields and boundary balls didn't help them along the way. South Africa Women now have to hope that they start well on Day 2 and restrict India under 650 if possible before they start climbing the mountain. That is it for today. Join us on Day 2 at 9.30 am IST (4 am GMT) and earlier for the build up. Till then, cheers!

Smriti Mandhana says she is happy how the day went. Credits the way Shafali Verma played and says it is a pleasure to see her play from the other end. Admits it is a remarkable achievement to get more than 500 runs. Tells the talk with Verma was to take on the bowlers, she took the seamers on and Verma targetted the spinners. Feels she is not sure about the target if it has ever happened in women's cricket.  Ends by saying the pitch started to turn a bit in the last hour.

An excellent way to begin the Test match. The hosts would be the happier side at the end of the day's play. Harmanpreet Kaur didn't hesitate as she chose to bat first and the openers didn't let the skipper down as the duo, Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana added 292 runs. Smriti Mandhana scored her third century in the last four international matches while Shafali Verma went onto score a century too. Verma though continued her merry way and converted it into double as her partner, Smriti Mandhana fell just one short of 150. Jemimah Rodrigues and Shafali Verma then added 86 runs before Verma was run out just after her double ton. Right now, India have Kaur and Ghosh in their 40s. India are in top position and one would say they have enough on the board but they'll try and tire out the visitors under scorching heat on Day 2 and look for a score around 650.

There was some movement in the first 10 overs and Verma and Smriti Mandhana respected it quite well but once the ball got soft and was coming onto the bat nicely, there was no looking back as both the openers scored runs briskly. Smriti Mandhana scored her fifty and Shafali Verma followed with her fourth Test fifty. Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma have scored 23 boundaries and a six overall and that tells you how the bowling has been so far. Ordinary! Just what we saw in the ODI format. South Africa Women have not learned their lessons and are paying the price. At this rate and the way they are bowling, it would be quite a long tiring day for the visitors. They'll hope the break brings some tactical plans out and a better way to kick off the second session. Stay tuned.
